From the path of allusion (ishara) in the verses, it has been said: ﴿Certainly the believers have succeeded﴾, i.e., they have reached the highest place, nearness and happiness; ﴿those who are humble in their prayer﴾, outwardly and inwardly. Humility outwardly is lowering the head, looking at the place of prostration and at what is before one, leaving turning around, tranquillity in the pillars, and the like. Humility inwardly is the calming of the soul from worldly thoughts and whisperings entirely, or leaving dwelling upon them, presence of heart with the meanings of the recitation and the remembrances, watching over the secret by leaving attention to created things, and the spirit being immersed in the sea of love. Humility is a condition for the validity of prayer according to some of the elite. al-Ghazali transmitted from Abu Talib al-Makki, from Bishr al-Hafi: "Whoever does not humble himself, his prayer is corrupt." This is also the view of some jurists, and its details are in their books. There is no disagreement that there is no reward for any saying or act of the prayer performed with heedlessness. How ugly is a worshipper who says ﴿All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Fatiha: 2] while he is heedless of the Lord, may He be exalted, and wholly turned toward the dirham and the dinar, then says ﴿You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help﴾ [al-Fatiha: 5], while there is nothing in his heart and mind other than these two. Such cases are numerous. From here al-Hasan said: "Every prayer in which the heart is not present, it is quicker toward punishment."

They have mentioned that prayer is the ascension of the believer. Whoever fabricates a prayer like this one is fit for that—far be it from Allah; whoever claims that has fabricated. ﴿And those who turn away from idle talk﴾. Some of them said: idle talk is everything that distracts from the Truth, Mighty and Majestic.

Abu Uthman said: everything in which the self has a share is idle talk. Abu Bakr ibn Tahir said: everything other than Allah the Exalted is idle talk. ﴿And those who are active in zakat﴾: it is the purification of the self from blameworthy character traits. ﴿And those who guard their private parts﴾, ﴿except over their wives or what their right hands possess, for they are not blameworthy﴾. This is an allusion to their mastery over the appetitive faculty, so they do not exceed in it what is prescribed for them. It has also been said: the allusion here is to the guarding of secrets, i.e., those who conceal from strangers the secrets whose disclosure is ugly, except before their peers and whoever is joined with them, or before their disciples who are like slaves to them. ﴿And those who are faithful to their trusts﴾: Muhammad ibn al-Fadl said: all their limbs, ﴿and their covenant﴾, the primordial covenant, ﴿they keep﴾. So they are good in deeds, words and beliefs. ﴿And those who are attentive to their prayers﴾, so they perform them with their conditions and do not do in them or after them anything that spoils them, such as showing off and self-admiration.

﴿And We certainly created man from an extract of clay﴾. It has been said that what was created from that is the sensible body, but the spirit is created from a divine light whose reality the intellects find it difficult to grasp. In His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Then We produced him as another creation. So blessed is Allah, the best of creators﴾ there is an allusion to the breathing of that created spirit from that light, and it is the human reality intended in the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Allah created Adam upon His image,"

i.e., upon His attributes, glorified is He, of being living, knowing, willing, powerful, and other attributes. ﴿And We created above you seven paths, and We were not heedless of creation﴾. This is an allusion to the levels of the self, some of which are above others, and each lower level veils the higher. Or it is an allusion to the veiling of the five outward senses and the two inward faculties of estimation and imagination. Other interpretations have also been given. ﴿And We sent down water from the sky﴾: it has been said, i.e., from the sky of care, water, i.e., the water of mercy, ﴿in measure﴾, i.e., according to the measure of the wayfarer's readiness, ﴿and We made it settle in the earth﴾, i.e., the earth of his existence, ﴿then We produced for you thereby gardens of palm trees﴾, i.e., palm trees of knowledge, ﴿and grapevines﴾, i.e., grapevines of unveilings. It has been said that the palm trees are an allusion to the sciences of the Sharia and the grapevines to the sciences of the Tariqa. ﴿For you therein are abundant fruits﴾: these are what exceeds the obligatory. ﴿And from them you eat﴾: an allusion to what is obligatory, without which the support of the Sharia and the Tariqa is not complete. ﴿And a tree that springs from Mount Sinai﴾: an allusion to the light that shines from the mountain of the heart through what it has obtained of

We ask Allah the Exalted to enable us to obey Him, to forgive us what we have committed of disobedience to Him, and to bestow upon us more than what we hope for of His mercy, out of honour for His noble Prophet and beloved, who is compassionate and merciful to the believers, may Allah the Exalted bless him, his family and companions, and grant peace, and exalt, honour and ennoble [him].
